inventoryPhotos.explanation: Inventory the camera-recorded metadata a small set of captured field photos declares about itself: JPEG frame width and height, IFD0 camera make, model and orientation code, and the ExifIFD capture wall time with its optional recorded UTC offset. Use it to reconcile photos with field observations in an editable workbook: it publishes a typed inventory.csv (feed it to Calc) and a metadata.json holding each photo's SHA-256, your stable ID and the scoped raw ExifTool observations. A separate independent byte-level reader must agree with ExifTool on every selected tag, and a second fresh ExifTool process must repeat the first. Missing tags stay explicit nulls; filesystem times are never used. It does not write, rotate or strip images, read GPS, faces or thumbnails, decode pixels, or certify when, where or by whom a photo was taken.
pitfalls: A camera can record a wrong clock, zone or orientation; agreement between ExifTool and the independent reader proves what the file says, not what happened.
capturedLocal is a wall time without a zone and is not UTC; capturedUtc exists only when the same file records OffsetTimeOriginal.
Orientation is the stored EXIF code 1-8; the pixels are not rotated.
Everything outside the nine selected fields, including GPS, is unassessed rather than absent; progressive, multi-image and non-baseline JPEGs are refused.
A Calc workbook handoff needs at least two photos and at least two present orientation codes.
An offset of -00:00 means an unknown offset and is refused; +00:00 is a recorded zero offset.

examples.purpose: Inventory four synthetic photos with mixed byte orders, offsets, missing tags and a formula-looking camera model.
Inventory two photos, one without any EXIF segment.
Hand the typed inventory.csv to Calc as an editable workbook.

inventoryPhotos.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

inspectMetadata.explanation: Read the camera-recorded metadata a set of photographs and XMP sidecars declares about itself into typed records: capture times and offsets, camera and lens identity, exposure, description, rights, GPS location and orientation. Each requested profile becomes a typed CSV that Calc can open as an editable workbook, and metadata.json keeps every source value, state and reconciliation for review. Independent host readers decode EXIF, GPS, IPTC and XMP from the captured bytes and are anchored against a fixed ExifTool listing; optionally the full native listing is published as native-observed evidence. It does not write, strip or decode images and certifies neither when, where nor by whom a photo was taken.
pitfalls: A camera or editor can record a wrong clock, zone, place or owner; agreement between readers proves what the file says, not what happened.
absent, unreadable, unsupported and ambiguous are different states; a null in the CSV has its reason in the State column.
Sources that disagree are reported, not resolved: no source is preferred and no Metadata Working Group precedence is applied.
GPS values are reported with the recorded datum text and no conversion; location, device identity and creator fields can identify people.
A native listing is verified only when a trusted ExifTool is configured to replay it.

examples.purpose: Inspect the capture, device and location profiles of a synthetic folder with an XMP sidecar pair.
Inspect explicit items with a pinned digest, a sidecar and the native listing.

inspectMetadata.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

auditMetadata.explanation: Audit the metadata of a media set against a closed rule set: required fields, conflicting or duplicated sources, malformed values, time plausibility (GPS UTC against the capture instant, digitization before capture), a privacy inventory of location, device and creator fields, and identical-content duplicates. Findings name the rule, item, field, state and evidence in audit.json and a typed findings.csv. It reports observations only: a clean audit is not certification, a finding is not proof of tampering, and nothing is changed or removed.
pitfalls: Findings are about recorded metadata, not about the photographed event.
privacyInventory lists what a file carries so you can decide; it does not make a file safe to share.
requiredFields needs require; timePlausibility needs a recorded offset to compare GPS and capture times.
Every audited field is read by the same independent decoders and anchored to ExifTool as inspectMetadata.

examples.purpose: Audit a synthetic set for required capture time and model, conflicts, unreadable values and privacy-relevant fields.

auditMetadata.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

compareMetadata.explanation: Compare the typed metadata of every item with one named baseline item, field by field: same, different, missing in the item, missing in the baseline, both absent or not comparable (ambiguous, unreadable or unsupported). Equality is exact on canonical values and nothing is rounded or preferred. differences.csv is a typed table for a workbook and comparison.json keeps each side's state and value.
pitfalls: Different is not wrong and same is not authentic; the baseline is only the reference you chose.
Fields outside the selected profiles and fields are not compared.
The baseline item must succeed; if it is faulted the run fails with INVALID_BASELINE.

examples.purpose: Compare device and description metadata of three synthetic photos with one baseline.

compareMetadata.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

editMetadata.explanation: Write new copies of photographs (a new copy of the same container: JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP or HEIF with existing Exif and XMP items) with their title, description, keywords, creator list, copyright, rights URL, rating, city or country set, cleared or (for keywords) added to and removed from. Every original is captured byte for byte and never modified; each output is published only after independent readback of every requested value or absence, a byte-for-byte comparison of the encoded image and everything that is not an editable metadata slot (for a JPEG its frame header, tables, scans and rendering segments; for another container an offset-free fingerprint of strips, tiles, chunks or items), and a native before/after diff that allows only the plan targets and declared side effects. Items that cannot be written are refused or fail individually with an outcome document at their stable artifact slot.
pitfalls: Not a way to write raw ExifTool tags: only the nine catalogue fields can be edited, by intent (set, clear, add, remove).
Text is exact: never normalised, trimmed, truncated or transliterated; a form that cannot hold it exactly is removed (or the item refused), never cut.
An existing IPTC character set is never changed over text it would reinterpret; legacy Latin-1 text keeps its meaning and the IPTC form of the edited field is removed and reported instead.
Proof P is about bytes, not pixels: it says nothing about image authenticity, provenance or how a program renders the picture.
Artifact slot i is the i-th item: a refused item keeps its slot as an outcome document (never an image), so binding that index to an image consumer fails instead of selecting another photo.

In a HEIF file only Exif and XMP items that already exist are edited; an edit that would create one is refused with HEIF_METADATA_ITEM_CREATION_UNSUPPORTED (a named limit of ExifTool 13.55 on the tested fixtures), and PNG, WebP and HEIF have no IPTC slot (declared loss iptcNotAvailableInContainer).

examples.purpose: Set a bilingual title, a two-line description, three creators, keywords, copyright, rights URL and rating on three photos, with a per-item description override.
Set the named city and country and clear keywords for every JPEG in a folder.
Add one keyword and remove another against the current concordant list.

editMetadata.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

removeMetadata.explanation: Write new copies of photographs (a new copy of the same container) with chosen categories of metadata removed: location (GPS and named places), capture time, device identity, descriptive text, creator and rights, and embedded thumbnails; or, alone, a rendering-preserving minimise for JPEG, PNG and WebP that deletes every EXIF, XMP, IPTC, Photoshop and text block and comment and keeps the encoded image, the rendering chunks or segments and the EXIF orientation, chroma position and colour space. TIFF and DNG minimise, thumbnails outside JPEG and every HEIF removal are named refusals. Native deletions are a closed list derived from the trusted listing of each capture, never authored and never a bare delete-all. Absence is proved by the independent readers and by a fresh native listing, the encoded image and rendering segments are proved byte-identical, and residual.json lists what remains with its limits.
pitfalls: This is removal of the listed categories in the understood locations, not anonymisation or privacy certification: file names, pixel content, unrecognised maker notes and embedded content remain.
An unrecognised maker note cannot be removed by ExifTool, so deviceIdentity refuses such a file; XMP structures that cannot be deleted without removing unrelated properties refuse the item.
Removing rights metadata can remove licence or attribution notices that may be legally required; the choice is yours.
Orientation, colour space, ICC, JFIF and Adobe segments are never removed, so a rotated photograph stays rotated.

A kept PNG, WebP or TIFF orientation stays: PNG-3 treats eXIf as a historical value, so a kept Orientation is preserved for viewers that honour it. A maker note and DNGPrivateData are kept and published as residuals.

examples.purpose: Remove location, capture time and thumbnails from a baseline and a progressive photo.
Remove descriptive text and creator and rights metadata from every JPEG in a folder.

removeMetadata.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

reconcileTime.explanation: Compare the capture clocks of photographs without writing anything: photos are grouped by the device that recorded them (or by your declaration), each group gets a skew (recorded minus true, in exact seconds) from the true times you declare for named photos, constant or linear-drift, and the report lists the capture time every photo would have if corrected, simultaneous-shot consistency and GPS time stamp cross-checks.
pitfalls: A true time is your declaration: a reference, an assumed offset or an assumeCorrect group is published as declared and never verified, so a tidy report is not proof that any clock was right.

Skew is estimated only from references you list; nothing is inferred from file times, GPS stamps or other photos, and a group without a reference is reported as having insufficient evidence rather than guessed.
No time zone, daylight-saving rule or leap second is known: a UTC instant exists only where the same file records an offset or you assumed one, and the report labels which.
Two bodies of one model without serial numbers are indistinguishable by recorded identity; group them by declaration instead.

A skew belongs to an instant: an item with no recorded or assumed offset gets no skew from a drift model, and a group anchored through simultaneity is reported conflicting when its own references contradict the path.
reconcileTime.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

examples.purpose: Report the skew of two cameras from one declared true time each and check three shots taken at the same moment.

locate.explanation: Report where photographs say they were taken without writing anything: latitude and longitude as exact signed decimal degrees summed from the stored rationals, the altitude with the height reference the file establishes, the recorded datum, and flags where sources disagree, with an optional approximate distance to a point you declare.
pitfalls: Stored precision is a serialisation property, not GPS accuracy; no position is verified, geocoded or converted between datums.

A legacy altitude reference 0 or 1 is reported as unspecified, not as sea level or ellipsoidal: only an Exif 3.x file (or a GPS-only 2.4 block) establishes the reference, and the edition evidence is published so you can see why.
compareTo distances are spherical (mean radius 6371008.8 m) and approximate; a recorded datum that differs from the declared one gives no distance.
locate.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

examples.purpose: Report the recorded positions and height references of three photos and their distance to a declared point.

correctTime.explanation: Write new copies (of the same container: JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP or HEIF with existing items) whose capture times are corrected by declared domain intent: a shift per camera clock group (days, hours, minutes and exact seconds), a skew derived from your true reference times, or a UTC offset with a keep rule (the instant or the wall clock). Every present EXIF, XMP and IPTC time of the selected fields moves together, proved by independent readback, byte-identical image data and a native before/after diff.
pitfalls: A correction is only as good as your declaration: references, assumed offsets and assumed-correct groups are not verified, and a corrected-looking time is not proof the clock was right.
GPS time stamps are the receiver's clock and are never shifted; maker-note, preview, sidecar and file-system times are neither read nor changed (see residual.json).
Selecting modified times moves a time that records an edit, not a capture; it is opt-in. Sources that disagree are refused by default.
A photo outside every correction group keeps its artifact slot as an unchanged copy or an outcome document, by policy; check each item's outcome, because a run can be partly successful.
Sub-seconds that IPTC cannot hold are truncated toward the earlier second and listed per item.
In TIFF and DNG the IPTC time pair is rewritten too; PNG, WebP and HEIF have no IPTC. A HEIF file whose Exif item does not exist is refused, not given one.
correctTime.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

examples.purpose: Shift one camera group by a declared hour and set the offset of another, keeping its instant.

setLocation.explanation: Write declared GPS positions into new copies of the same container (JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP or HEIF with an existing Exif item): latitude and longitude as signed decimal degrees exactly as declared, an optional altitude with an explicit ellipsoidal or sea-level reference, the datum and a horizontal error text, with declared handling of stale GPS and XMP companions and of altitudes the file's metadata edition cannot express.
pitfalls: Positions are your declaration, not a measurement: nothing is verified or geocoded, and place names (IPTC city, XMP location) are not updated.
The 2e-10 degree bound is how precisely the stored rationals hold your decimal, not the accuracy of the position.

An altitude is written only with the reference you declare and only where the edition can express it; there is no vertical datum conversion and no ExifVersion promotion. Writing that would change the meaning of an untouched height is refused for that item.
Removing stale companions (direction, speed, time stamps, XMP positions) is planned before the write; keeping them can leave a direction that no longer matches the position.
A TIFF, DNG, PNG or WebP without an Exif block gets one when the policy allows; a HEIF file never gets a new Exif item (HEIF_METADATA_ITEM_CREATION_UNSUPPORTED).
setLocation.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

examples.purpose: Write declared positions, one with a sea-level altitude, and remove stale direction metadata.

geotagFromTrack.explanation: Geotag photographs into new copies of the same container from GPX tracks: each photo is placed at its capture instant by great-circle interpolation between consecutive timed fixes of a validated track, using the recorded or declared offset and an optional declared clock correction, with gap, overlap, speed and endpoint rules, a track report, a geotag plan and independent proofs. The native geotag feature is never used.
pitfalls: The photo instant depends on the camera clock and offset: a wrong clock gives a wrong position, so reconcile and correct the clock first or declare the correction.

The path between fixes is unknown: interpolation is a straight great-circle estimate, no accuracy or confidence is claimed, and nothing is extrapolated, bridged across a gap or taken from another segment or track.

GPX is untrusted XML: DTDs, entities and external references are refused, zoneless times need an explicit rule, and invalid points are refused or excluded by policy. WGS-84 is assumed for GPX 1.1 only; a GPX 1.0 datum must be declared.
A photo that cannot be placed is copied unchanged or refused by policy with its reason; check each item's outcome, because a run can be partly successful.

A correctTime plan used as the clock correction moves the placement instant by the plan's own before and after states (an offset kept to the instant moves nothing; one kept to the wall clock moves it); an item the plan could not correct is refused rather than placed on its uncorrected time.
geotagFromTrack.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

examples.purpose: Place three photos on a synthetic GPX track with a declared one-hour clock correction and a stated maximum gap.

copyMetadata.explanation: Carry selected kinds of information from a source onto new copies of JPEG, TIFF, DNG, PNG, WebP and HEIF photos as typed values (any item can be the source), with exact text and rational pairs, declared conflict, absence and loss policies, and independent readback, byte-identical image data, a native before/after diff and a source-versus-output proof for every copy. Nothing is copied as a block.
pitfalls: Selected typed values only: MakerNotes, unknown tags, thumbnails and XMP structures are not copied, and the capture time and location groups are carried through the E3 writers, alone or in any union with the other groups.
A copy never creates an Exif block or ExifIFD; a destination without one is refused per item, because creating it would change what an untouched GPS-only height means.
Device serial numbers identify physical equipment and are carried only when you select them.

A destination container without an IPTC slot (PNG, WebP, HEIF) declares the loss iptcNotAvailableInContainer instead of creating a carrier, and a HEIF destination without the needed Exif or XMP item is refused.
copyMetadata.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

applySidecar.explanation: Apply the information in each photo's XMP sidecar to a new copy of the photo: the same typed transfer as copyMetadata with the sidecar as the source. The sidecar is captured, hashed and anchored, never modified and never copied; an item without one is reported and the others continue.
pitfalls: Only the values the sidecar actually records are applied; absent in the sidecar is a decision of the absent policy, never a guess. Existing sidecars are never merged or edited.
ExifTool lists some sidecar properties it does not interpret (the altitude reference): the transfer reads them with Schemaxis's own reader.
Without a sidecar for an item the item is reported and the others continue.
applySidecar.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

exportSidecar.explanation: Write a portable XMP sidecar of selected kinds of information for each photo from its typed snapshot, in a closed set of 29 properties, with exact text, exact rational pairs, an explicit altitude reference rule, stated coordinate quantisation and declared losses. Each sidecar is proved by re-serialising, re-reading with the hardened reader and a fresh native listing.
pitfalls: The sidecar holds selected present facts only; it is not a copy of the photo's metadata and it does not preserve MakerNotes or unknown tags.
A sidecar altitude with sea-level reference code 2 is read by ExifTool 13.55 with the sign inverted (its Composite uses legacy 0/1 meanings); the report carries that residual.
Native agreement shows a property is present and parseable, not that ExifTool interprets it.
exportSidecar.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

planNames.explanation: Plan what each photo would be called and which folder it would go in, from recorded capture time and camera text, with a closed token vocabulary, a declared sanitiser and collision rules, and a deterministic name plan and table. Nothing is renamed or copied.
pitfalls: Names come from recorded capture facts, which can be wrong; a plan does not certify when or where a photo was taken.
The sanitiser targets portable names; a destination file system can still apply its own rules, and collisions outside the run are out of scope.
A plan is valid only for the captured bytes it lists.
planNames.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

organiseCopies.explanation: Make a named, foldered set of exact byte copies of photos (and optionally their adjacent sidecars) inside the run, from an inline name rule or a planNames document, with a stale-plan check, create-only copying, fixed artifact slots and a tree proof that every copy equals its capture.
pitfalls: Copies stay inside the run directory; there is no delivery elsewhere and no archive.
A plan made for other bytes is refused as stale; an unrelated sidecar is never matched by name alone.
Organising is not privacy or provenance certification: the copies carry all the original metadata.
organiseCopies.question: When would you choose this operation, what does it produce, and what assumptions matter?

fields.explanation: A request to read, audit, compare, edit or remove photo metadata: inventoryPhotos (the fixed selected-field inventory of 1 to 16 baseline JPEGs), inspectMetadata, auditMetadata and compareMetadata over a media set of photos and XMP sidecars, and editMetadata and removeMetadata, which write new copies. Results are observed or proved metadata for a person to review; they are not certified capture time, location, authorship or privacy.

/properties/version.explanation: Required document contract schemaxis.exiftool/1. It names the authored JSON model, independently of the configured ExifTool release.

/properties/operation.explanation: Select one of the sixteen operations: inventoryPhotos, inspectMetadata, auditMetadata, compareMetadata, editMetadata, removeMetadata, reconcileTime, locate, correctTime, setLocation, geotagFromTrack, copyMetadata, applySidecar, exportSidecar, planNames or organiseCopies. No ExifTool option, tag name, tag list, configuration file, expression, template or script can be authored: you name catalogue fields, groups and domain intent, and the adaptor chooses fixed native commands.

/properties/photos.explanation: The photos to inventory, in the order you want rows (1 to 16). Order is preserved in inventory.csv and metadata.json. Each photo is captured into the run before ExifTool starts; total size is at most 16MiB. Each entry must be a different source file: the same path, an alias or a hard link is refused (identical bytes in distinct files are allowed and not deduplicated).

/properties/photos/items.explanation: One photo: a stable ID, an absolute local JPEG path and an optional SHA-256 pin. Duplicate IDs and any malformed JPEG or selected tag refuse this exact photo before ExifTool runs.

/properties/photos/items/properties/id.explanation: Your stable human link for the photo and its row key: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter, unique in the document. It is published; the file path never is.

/properties/photos/items/properties/path.explanation: Absolute local path of one regular baseline sequential 8-bit three-component JPEG/JFIF (.jpg or .jpeg), at most 8MiB, without parent references. Symbolic links, other formats, progressive or multi-image files are refused.

/properties/photos/items/properties/sha2.explanation: Optional lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 pin for the photo bytes. A mismatch is refused as PHOTO_HASH_MISMATCH; omit it to record the captured digest without pinning.

/properties/media.explanation: The set of photographs and XMP sidecar files to read: either an explicit list of items or one folder. Every item is captured into the run before any native process starts, and every scanned folder entry is listed in manifest.json as included or excluded with a reason, so you can see exactly which files were and were not examined.
/properties/media.defaultMeaning: Required: there is no default media set.
pitfalls: A folder that changes while it is captured fails with MEDIA_FOLDER_CHANGED rather than producing a different set than you authored.
Excluded files (extension, hidden, symlink, too large, count limit, ambiguous sidecar) make the set status partial; they are never silently dropped.

/properties/media/anyOf/0.explanation: Explicit items: 1 to 512 entries, each with a stable ID and an absolute path. Order is preserved in every publication. A bad item becomes an item fault and the rest continue; if every item fails the run fails.

/properties/media/anyOf/0/properties/ite.explanation: The explicit item list, 1 to 512 entries in the order you want rows. Each entry must be a different source file: the same path, an alias or a hard link is refused for the later entry.

One item: a stable ID, an absolute .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .dng, .png, .webp, .heic, .heif, .avif or .xmp path (the container is detected by signature, never by suffix), an optional SHA-256 pin and, for a photo, an optional XMP sidecar path. A problem with this item faults only this item.

Your stable human link for the item and its row key: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter, unique in the set. It is published; compareMetadata names its baseline by this ID.

Absolute local path of one regular photo file without parent references: .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .dng, .png, .webp, .heic, .heif, .avif (the container is detected by signature, never by suffix) or a standalone .xmp. Symbolic links, files over 64 MiB (256 MiB for a name ending .tif, .tiff or .dng) and missing files fault this item. The file is only read, never written.
Optional pin: 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits of the expected file bytes. A different file at the same path faults this item with PHOTO_HASH_MISMATCH instead of being read as the pinned one.
/properties/media/anyOf/0/properties/ite.defaultMeaning: Without a pin the bytes captured now are accepted and recorded.

/properties/media/anyOf/0/properties/ite.explanation: Optional absolute path of an XMP sidecar (.xmp) for a photo item. Its properties are read as a separate source, so embedded and sidecar values that disagree make the field ambiguous. A standalone .xmp item cannot have a sidecar.
/properties/media/anyOf/0/properties/ite.defaultMeaning: No sidecar: only metadata embedded in the file is read.

/properties/media/anyOf/1.explanation: A folder scanned deterministically: names in byte order, no symbolic link followed, hidden entries skipped, never leaving the selected root. Every scanned entry appears in manifest.json with a reason when excluded.

/properties/media/anyOf/1/properties/fol.explanation: The folder to scan and its declared limits. Item IDs are derived from file stems (characters outside letters, digits and underscore become underscores); a stem that cannot form an ID or repeats an earlier ID is excluded with a reason.
Absolute local path of a real directory (not a link) without parent references. Files inside are only read.
Which file types become items: .jpg, .jpeg and/or .xmp. A listed type that is absent from the folder is simply not found; an entry with another extension is excluded with reason extension.
One file extension, lower case with its dot: .jpg, .jpeg or .xmp; matching ignores case.
How many directory levels below the folder are scanned, 0 (only the folder) to 2. Deeper directories are listed as directory-beyond-depth and not entered.
/properties/media/anyOf/1/properties/fol.defaultMeaning: 1: the folder and its immediate subfolders.

/properties/media/anyOf/1/properties/fol.explanation: At most this many items are taken, in sorted path order; further eligible files are excluded with reason count-limit and make the set status partial. At most 512.
adjacent pairs an image with name.xmp or name.jpg.xmp next to it (two candidates make it ambiguous and exclude both); none treats every .xmp as its own item when .xmp is listed.

/properties/profiles.explanation: Which groups of catalogued fields to assess: capture, device, exposure, description, rights, location and rendering. Fields outside the selected profiles are unassessed, neither read nor claimed absent. inspectMetadata writes one typed CSV per profile.
/properties/profiles.defaultMeaning: Required for inspectMetadata; optional for audit and compare, which also assess the fields they name or need.

/properties/profiles/items.explanation: One profile name from the closed list. The profile decides which catalogue fields are assessed; see the field catalogue for each field's meaning, units, absence, privacy and proof level.

/properties/nativeListing.explanation: When true, also publish ExifTool's complete fixed listing of every captured file as native-observations.json (native-observed proof level). Verifying such a run needs a configured trusted ExifTool to replay it, otherwise verification reports NATIVE_REPLAY_UNAVAILABLE.
/properties/nativeListing.defaultMeaning: false: the native run only anchors the independent values and nothing native-observed is published.

/properties/require.explanation: Catalogue fields that every item must record. Each item for which one is not present gets a requiredFields finding naming the state (absent, unreadable, unsupported, ambiguous). Requires the requiredFields rule.
/properties/require.defaultMeaning: No required fields; requiredFields is then not part of the default rules.

/properties/require/items.explanation: One catalogue field ID, for example capturedLocal or cameraModel. IDs are catalogue names, not ExifTool tag names.

/properties/rules.explanation: Which audit rules to apply: requiredFields, sourceConflicts, unreadableValues, timePlausibility, privacyInventory and duplicateContent. Rules only report; none changes a file or certifies one.
/properties/rules.defaultMeaning: Every rule, with requiredFields only when require is given.

/properties/rules/items.explanation: One audit rule name from the closed list.

/properties/gpsToleranceSeconds.explanation: The largest difference between the GPS UTC stamp and the capture instant that timePlausibility accepts without a finding. Meaningful only with that rule.

/properties/baseline.explanation: The ID of the item every other item is compared with. It must be an authored item ID (explicit items) or an ID derived from a folder file stem, and its own item must succeed.
pitfalls: Which item is the baseline decides what counts as different; neither side is treated as correct.

/properties/fields.explanation: Extra catalogue fields to compare beyond those in the selected profiles.
/properties/fields.defaultMeaning: Only the fields of the selected profiles.

/properties/fields/items.explanation: One catalogue field ID. IDs are catalogue names, not ExifTool tag names.

/oneOf/0.explanation: Inventory variant: the original fixed selected-field inventory of 1 to 16 baseline JPEG photos (operation inventoryPhotos), with photos as the only content field.

/oneOf/0/properties/version.explanation: Use schemaxis.exiftool/1; it covers every ExifTool operation. It names the authored JSON model, independently of the configured ExifTool release.

/oneOf/0/properties/operation.explanation: Fixed to inventoryPhotos in this variant, which decides which other fields are accepted.

/oneOf/0/properties/photos.explanation: The photos to inventory, in the order you want rows (1 to 16). Order is preserved in inventory.csv and metadata.json. Each photo is captured into the run before ExifTool starts; total size is at most 16MiB. Each entry must be a different source file: the same path, an alias or a hard link is refused (identical bytes in distinct files are allowed and not deduplicated).

/oneOf/0/properties/photos/items.explanation: One photo: a stable ID, an absolute local JPEG path and an optional SHA-256 pin. Duplicate IDs and any malformed JPEG or selected tag refuse this exact photo before ExifTool runs.

/oneOf/0/properties/photos/items/propert.explanation: Your stable human link for the photo and its row key: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter, unique in the document. It is published; the file path never is.

Absolute local path of one regular baseline sequential 8-bit three-component JPEG/JFIF (.jpg or .jpeg), at most 8MiB, without parent references. Symbolic links, other formats, progressive or multi-image files are refused.
Optional lowercase 64-hex SHA-256 pin for the photo bytes. A mismatch is refused as PHOTO_HASH_MISMATCH; omit it to record the captured digest without pinning.

/oneOf/1.explanation: Inspect variant: operation inspectMetadata over a media set, with the profiles to assess and optionally the native listing.

/oneOf/1/properties/version.explanation: Use schemaxis.exiftool/1; it covers every ExifTool operation. It names the authored JSON model, independently of the configured ExifTool release.

/oneOf/1/properties/operation.explanation: Fixed to inspectMetadata in this variant, which decides which other fields are accepted.

/oneOf/1/properties/media.explanation: The set of photographs and XMP sidecar files to read: either an explicit list of items or one folder. Every item is captured into the run before any native process starts, and every scanned folder entry is listed in manifest.json as included or excluded with a reason, so you can see exactly which files were and were not examined.
/oneOf/1/properties/media.defaultMeaning: Required: there is no default media set.

Excluded files (extension, hidden, symlink, too large, count limit, ambiguous sidecar) make the set status partial; they are never silently dropped.

Your stable human link for the item and its row key: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter, unique in the set. It is published; compareMetadata names its baseline by this ID.

Absolute local path of one regular photo file without parent references: .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .dng, .png, .webp, .heic, .heif, .avif (the container is detected by signature, never by suffix) or a standalone .xmp. One file extension, lower case with its dot: .jpg, .jpeg or .xmp; matching ignores case.

adjacent pairs an image with name.xmp or name.jpg.xmp next to it (two candidates make it ambiguous and exclude both); none treats every .xmp as its own item when .xmp is listed.

removeCompanion (default) deletes a companion IPTC or EXIF form that cannot hold the new value exactly and reports it; refuse refuses the item instead. Values are never truncated or transliterated and the XMP value is always complete.

/oneOf/5.explanation: The removeMetadata form of the document: the properties it accepts and requires.

/oneOf/5/properties/version.explanation: Required document contract schemaxis.exiftool/1. It names the authored JSON model, independently of the configured ExifTool release.

Excluded files (extension, hidden, symlink, too large, count limit, ambiguous sidecar) make the set status partial; they are never silently dropped.

Absolute local path of one regular photo file without parent references: .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .dng, .png, .webp, .heic, .heif, .avif (the container is detected by signature, never by suffix) or a standalone .xmp. /oneOf/5/properties/media/anyOf/0/proper.defaultMeaning: Without a pin the bytes captured now are accepted and recorded.

/oneOf/5/properties/media/anyOf/0/proper.explanation: Optional absolute path of an XMP sidecar (.xmp) for a photo item. Its properties are read as a separate source, so embedded and sidecar values that disagree make the field ambiguous. A standalone .xmp item cannot have a sidecar.

Item IDs belonging to this group; each media item belongs to exactly one declared group.

Free text recorded with the reference (for example how the true time was known). It is published, never interpreted.

/properties/maxDriftRate.explanation: The largest drift rate the linearDrift model accepts, in seconds of skew per second (above 0, at most 0.01).

/properties/maxDriftExtrapolationSeconds.explanation: How far outside the span of its references a group's drift may be extended, in seconds (0 to 86400). Outside it the item is reported, not silently extrapolated.

/properties/compareTo/properties/longitu.explanation: Longitude of the point in signed decimal degrees as text (east positive).

/properties/compareTo/properties/datum.explanation: The datum of the point (for example WGS-84). Without it no distance is published to a photo whose recorded datum differs or is missing.

references derives the group skew from your declared references and corrects the group by that amount.
A shift added to the recorded time of every photo of the group: any combination of days, hours, minutes and exact decimal seconds, negative or positive.
Days to add (negative to subtract), a calendar-day count with no time zone rules.

Change the UTC offset recorded with the times of the group, with an explicit rule for what stays fixed.

/oneOf/10/properties/version.explanation: Required document contract schemaxis.exiftool/1. It names the authored JSON model, independently of the configured ExifTool release.

/oneOf/10/properties/operation.explanation: Place photos from GPX tracks into new copies (geotagFromTrack). No ExifTool option, tag name, configuration, expression or script can be authored: you declare domain intent (devices, true times, positions, tracks) and the adaptor computes fixed numeric assignments, which it declares in the plan.

/oneOf/10/properties/media.explanation: The set of photographs and XMP sidecar files to read: either an explicit list of items or one folder. Every item is captured into the run before any native process starts, and every scanned folder entry is listed in manifest.json as included or excluded with a reason, so you can see exactly which files were and were not examined.
/oneOf/10/properties/media.defaultMeaning: Required: there is no default media set.
pitfalls: A folder that changes while it is captured fails with MEDIA_FOLDER_CHANGED rather than producing a different set than you authored.
Excluded files (extension, hidden, symlink, too large, count limit, ambiguous sidecar) make the set status partial; they are never silently dropped.

/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/0.explanation: Explicit items: 1 to 512 entries, each with a stable ID and an absolute path. Order is preserved in every publication. A bad item becomes an item fault and the rest continue; if every item fails the run fails.

/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/0/prope.explanation: The explicit item list, 1 to 512 entries in the order you want rows. Each entry must be a different source file: the same path, an alias or a hard link is refused for the later entry.

One item: a stable ID, an absolute .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .dng, .png, .webp, .heic, .heif, .avif or .xmp path (the container is detected by signature, never by suffix), an optional SHA-256 pin and, for a photo, an optional XMP sidecar path. A problem with this item faults only this item.

Your stable human link for the item and its row key: 1 to 32 ASCII letters, digits or underscores starting with a letter, unique in the set. It is published; compareMetadata names its baseline by this ID.

Absolute local path of one regular photo file without parent references: .jpg, .jpeg, .tif, .tiff, .dng, .png, .webp, .heic, .heif, .avif (the container is detected by signature, never by suffix) or a standalone .xmp. Symbolic links, files over 64 MiB (256 MiB for a name ending .tif, .tiff or .dng) and missing files fault this item. The file is only read, never written.
Optional pin: 64 lowercase hexadecimal digits of the expected file bytes. A different file at the same path faults this item with PHOTO_HASH_MISMATCH instead of being read as the pinned one.
/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/0/prope.defaultMeaning: Without a pin the bytes captured now are accepted and recorded.

/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/0/prope.explanation: Optional absolute path of an XMP sidecar (.xmp) for a photo item. Its properties are read as a separate source, so embedded and sidecar values that disagree make the field ambiguous. A standalone .xmp item cannot have a sidecar.
/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/0/prope.defaultMeaning: No sidecar: only metadata embedded in the file is read.

/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/1.explanation: A folder scanned deterministically: names in byte order, no symbolic link followed, hidden entries skipped, never leaving the selected root. Every scanned entry appears in manifest.json with a reason when excluded.

/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/1/prope.explanation: The folder to scan and its declared limits. Item IDs are derived from file stems (characters outside letters, digits and underscore become underscores); a stem that cannot form an ID or repeats an earlier ID is excluded with a reason.
Absolute local path of a real directory (not a link) without parent references. Files inside are only read.
Which file types become items: .jpg, .jpeg and/or .xmp. A listed type that is absent from the folder is simply not found; an entry with another extension is excluded with reason extension.
One file extension, lower case with its dot: .jpg, .jpeg or .xmp; matching ignores case.
How many directory levels below the folder are scanned, 0 (only the folder) to 2. Deeper directories are listed as directory-beyond-depth and not entered.
/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/1/prope.defaultMeaning: 1: the folder and its immediate subfolders.

/oneOf/10/properties/media/anyOf/1/prope.explanation: At most this many items are taken, in sorted path order; further eligible files are excluded with reason count-limit and make the set status partial. At most 512.
adjacent pairs an image with name.xmp or name.jpg.xmp next to it (two candidates make it ambiguous and exclude both); none treats every .xmp as its own item when .xmp is listed.

/oneOf/10/properties/apply.explanation: write (default) writes the new copies and publishes the plan with the report; plan publishes the plan and the reports without writing any copy. The plan can be applied later with the plan option, and only to the captures it was made for.

/oneOf/10/properties/tracks.explanation: The GPX track files the photos are placed on (1 to 8). Each is captured byte for byte before any parsing and its SHA-256 is recorded in the plan.

/oneOf/10/properties/tracks/items.explanation: One GPX file with a stable ID.

/oneOf/10/properties/tracks/items/proper.explanation: A stable name for the track (letters, digits, underscores).
Absolute local path of a GPX 1.0 or 1.1 file (at most 32 MiB; 64 MiB for all tracks). DTDs, entities and external references are refused.
Optional pin: the run is refused if the captured file does not have this SHA-256.

/oneOf/10/properties/photoTime.explanation: How the instant of each photo is derived from its recorded capture wall time: the capture time minus the recorded (or assumed) offset, moved by a declared clock correction that applies to the placement only. The photo's own time fields are not rewritten.

/oneOf/10/properties/photoTime/propertie.explanation: captured: the recorded capture time (the only source).

The UTC offset to assume for groups whose files record no offset (or whose recorded offset you do not trust). The instant derived from an assumed offset is labelled assumed; a recorded but unreadable or conflicting offset is not treated as absent.
One assumption: a group and the offset its photos were taken at.
The group the assumption applies to (at most one assumed offset per group).
The assumed UTC offset as +HH:MM or -HH:MM. -00:00 and other forms are handled exactly as the specification of each protocol states.

none (default) uses the recorded times as they are; otherwise per-group shifts, or the plan file of a correctTime run (which carries its own shifts), move the placement instants without changing the photos' own times.
A declared correction: per-group shifts, or the plan file of a correctTime run, which carries its own reviewed shifts.
Group shifts applied to the placement instants.
The group the shift applies to.
The shift added to the recorded time of the group's photos.
Seconds to add as an exact decimal text (negative to subtract).
Absolute path of a time-correction plan published by correctTime; its group shifts are applied to the placement instants.

/oneOf/10/properties/groups.explanation: How photos are grouped into camera clocks. By default photos are grouped by the exact recorded make, model and body serial text; declare members to group by your own names instead (for example two bodies of one model). /oneOf/10/properties/groups.defaultMeaning: recordedDevice with the keys cameraMake, cameraModel and bodySerialNumber.

/oneOf/10/properties/groups/properties/b.explanation: recordedDevice groups by recorded identity text; declared groups by the members you list (every media item must belong to exactly one declared group).

/oneOf/10/properties/groups/properties/k.explanation: Which recorded identity fields make up the group key. A field that is missing or ambiguous in a file is reported as such and never merged or guessed.
One identity field: cameraMake, cameraModel or bodySerialNumber.

/oneOf/10/properties/groups/properties/m.explanation: Declared groups and their member item IDs; only valid with by: declared.
One declared group: its name and its member items.
The group name (a letter then letters, digits or underscores, at most 32 characters). Names of the form dev followed by digits are reserved for recorded-device groups.
Item IDs belonging to this group; each media item belongs to exactly one declared group.

/oneOf/10/properties/groups/properties/i.explanation: Move individual photos to a named recorded-device group when their recorded identity is missing or wrong (for example a body serial number the camera did not write).
One override: an item and the group it belongs to.
The media item ID to move.
The group the item joins. It may join an existing recorded-device group (devN) that the report publishes; inventing a reserved devN name is refused.

/oneOf/10/properties/interpolation.explanation: Limits on placing a photo between track fixes. Defaults are conservative: no snapping, a 300 second gap limit and a 5 metre overlap agreement.

/oneOf/10/properties/interpolation/prope.explanation: The largest time between two consecutive fixes across which a photo may be interpolated (1 to 3600 seconds). A longer gap leaves the photo unplaced with a reason.
A photo this close in time (0 to 60 seconds) to the end of a segment may snap to that endpoint instead of being unplaced. 0 means never snap.
When overlapping tracks both cover the photo instant, every pair of candidate positions must agree within this distance (metres, decimal text) or the photo is refused with the conflict.

/oneOf/10/properties/track.explanation: How the GPX content is read: invalid points, times without a zone, elevation and the datum of a GPX 1.0 file.

/oneOf/10/properties/track/properties/in.explanation: refuse (default) fails the track on a point with an invalid coordinate or time; exclude drops such points and lists them in the track report.

/oneOf/10/properties/track/properties/zo.explanation: How to read a track time without a zone designator: asSchema (default) follows the GPX schema rule, refuse refuses the track, utc reads it as UTC and labels that.

/oneOf/10/properties/track/properties/el.explanation: ignore (default) never writes an altitude from the track; an object with a reference writes the interpolated elevation with that declared reference. The GPX schema does not say which vertical reference an elevation has, so you declare it.
Use track elevations with a declared vertical reference.
seaLevel or ellipsoidal: the vertical reference you declare for the track's elevations.

/oneOf/10/properties/track/properties/da.explanation: The horizontal datum of a GPX 1.0 file (which has a datum element only in some producers); required knowledge you declare. GPX 1.1 is WGS-84 by its schema.

/oneOf/10/properties/policies/properties.explanation: remove (default) deletes GPS values that no longer match the new position (direction, speed, time stamps and similar) and lists each removal in the plan; keep leaves them and says so.
ifPresent (default) updates XMP positions only where the file has them; always writes them; remove deletes them. XMP text is written exactly as the decimal you declared.

allow (default) may create the Exif or GPS directory a file lacks; refuse refuses such items. Creating an Exif directory can add mandatory tags and change how an untouched altitude is read, so the typed height proof refuses a change of meaning.
refuse (default) refuses an item whose edition cannot express the declared altitude reference; omitAltitude writes the position without the altitude and says so.
true removes the recorded image direction, which no longer matches a new position; false leaves it.
copyUnchanged (default) copies a photo that gets no position unchanged to its slot and reports the reason; refuseSlot publishes an outcome document at that slot instead of a copy.
photoInstant (default) writes the GPS date and time stamps from the photo instant used for the placement; none writes no stamp. The stamp is a derived value and does not claim the receiver clock.
Refuse a placement when the track implies a speed above this between the neighbouring fixes (metres per second, at most 1000). A sanity bound for bad fixes, not an accuracy claim.

ifPresent (default) writes IPTC only into files that already have an IPTC block; always creates one, declares UTF-8 and refreshes the IPTC digest. XMP is always written; EXIF only where an Exif segment exists.
